title: In a short exact sequence, a bound n on the middle term and n+1 on the quotient bound the submodule by n
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $m\ge0$ an integer and $0\to M'\xrightarrow{u}M\xrightarrow{v}M''\to0$ a short exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] ($u$ injective, $v$ surjective, $\operatorname{Im}u=\operatorname{Ker}v$). Assume that $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le m$ and that $M''$ has a projective resolution of length $\le m+1$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] (exact sequences $0\to P_m\to\dots\to P_0\to M\to0$ and $0\to Q_{m+1}\to\dots\to Q_0\to M''\to0$ with all $P_i$, $Q_i$ projective $R$-modules). Then $M'$ has a projective resolution of length $\le m$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065S (lemma-exact-sequence-projective-dimension, line 26762), part (1). Tag verified in tags/tags: 065S,algebra-lemma-exact-sequence-projective-dimension

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $R$-module $N$ and set $i=m+1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-ext-characterization] (Stacks 065R), the assumed resolution of $M$ of length $\le m$ makes $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(M,N)=0$. Applying the same characterization with $n=m+1$ to the assumed resolution of $M''$ gives $\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_R(M'',N)=0$. Here $i\ge1$, including when $m=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065S (lemma-exact-sequence-projective-dimension), proof invoking Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext)

proof.text: For the given short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-first-variable] (Stacks 065P) gives an exact segment $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(M,N)\xrightarrow{u^*}\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(M',N)\xrightarrow{\delta^i}\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}_R(M'',N)$. Both outer groups vanish by Step 1. Thus $\ker(\delta^i)=\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(M',N)=\operatorname{im}(u^*)=0$; hence $\operatorname{Ext}^{m+1}_R(M',N)=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065S (lemma-exact-sequence-projective-dimension), proof invoking Lemma Tag 065P (lemma-reverse-long-exact-seq-ext)

proof.text: Because $N$ was arbitrary, [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-ext-characterization] (Stacks 065R), now in its Ext-vanishing-to-resolution direction with $X=M'$ and $n=m$, supplies a projective resolution of $M'$ of length $\le m$, as claimed.
